result.note: Tests the UPI merchant-fee amendments, the export-only inventory rule for foreign-invested e-commerce, and the electronics tax holiday extension; avoids the Lok Sabha passage date, which the story gives inconsistently.

questions.prompt: In August 2026, the Finance Minister tabled amendments creating a legal framework to reintroduce merchant fees on UPI transactions. Consider the following statements:
items: The proposed fee of 0.3 to 0.5% would apply to UPI payments above INR 2,000 made to larger merchants.
UPI transactions above INR 2,000 account for about two-thirds of transaction volume but only 4% of value.
The Lok Sabha passed the amendments by voice vote, and they still await the Rajya Sabha.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 2 reverses the figures. Transactions above INR 2,000 are just 4% of volume but 67% of value. The Lok Sabha passed the bill without debate a day after the RBI governor called the discussion premature.
questions.source: Transactions above that threshold are just 4% of volume but 67% of value.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about the change to e-commerce rules announced by India in August 2026:
items: Foreign-invested e-commerce platforms may hold inventory in India for goods bound for export, routed through a registered Exporter-on-Record.
The decade-old ban on foreign-owned inventory for domestic sales was lifted.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explain: Delhi did not touch the decade-old ban on foreign-owned domestic inventory. It gave Amazon and Flipkart the right to hold inventory only for exports, and Amazon linked the move to its USD 80 billion export target for 2030.
questions.source: India let foreign-invested e-commerce platforms hold inventory domestically, but only for goods bound for export, routed through a registered Exporter-on-Record.

questions.prompt: In August 2026, Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman introduced a bill proposing to extend the tax holiday for electronics manufacturers. Up to which year would the tax holiday be extended?
questions.explain: The bill would push the tax holiday from 2031 to 2040-41. The same bill would ease approvals for global cloud providers and let fund managers relocate to India without subjecting offshore funds to Indian tax laws.
questions.source: extend the tax holiday for electronics manufacturers' from 2031 to 2040-41, ease approvals for global cloud providers
